searchText: altair on prater looking good (?) Seeing a fair few missed blocks beaconcha.in seems to be lagging? or did something happen? sync committee aggregates coming in around 70% looking into it ``time="2021-09-02 12:24:56" level=warning msg="Received message from outdated fork digest 0x79df0428" prefix=sync topic="/eth2/79df0428/beacon_aggregate_and_proof/ssz_snappy"`` got a bunch of those around the fork time i assume older clients that are not altair compatible? correct so altair on prater success ? Success in that it works and everyone on same chain But some issues did arise that have been patched or are under investigation the list (from my memory): * teku made a bad block(s) -- issue self healed after 1 epoch and we know the problem. simple once found but tricky * prysm launched without optimization flags and was seeing longer than expected times to produce block (think close to 1s instead of 300ms). optimizations are now deployed * lighthouse was also seeing longer than expected block production times. not theory yet. australia went to sleep * some very low sync committee blocks (e.g. 1% instead of 70%+) * general lower than expected sync committee participation -- the missing bits are consistent block to block so seems like a systemic issue with a client or node rather than an issue with the algorithm. being investigated First of all thank you so much for such a thorough update!! <@291925846556540928> Did the sync committee problems not manifest themselves on Pyrmont earlier last month? Looking at pyrmont, the same pattern of slightly lower than optimal (10 to 15%) participation is present but the random drops to near zero are not I'd expect a slight drop on participation because anything beyond perfect inclusion distance gets dropped, and we definitely don't see perfect inclusion distance for attestations, particularly on prater. Ah, but it is always the same bits that are not included! I supoose they could be the set of nodes with timing issues or somethng but its suspicious Are you converting bits to validators? I checked the first committee on pyrmont and most of the bits that were consistently not validating were also inactive in regular attestations I havent done more than a cursory inspection. The fact that pyrmont has 85% activity but only gets roughly 70% on each sync committee and that it is consistent on each block across a sync assignment implies there are online vals that are consistently not doing the sync job well But a programmatic analysis is needed. Havent had a chance to dig As opposed to instead an issue in aggregation that would scatter the failures about the committee more Right, we're talking about more than 75 validators then from the 512, so I suppose that's really statistically relevant and not a bad sample from one committee only. I'm a bit shocked though cause I grabbed the state on pyrmont and went checking validator by validator who wasn't participating in the sync committee and gave up around the 10th that they were all leaking previously

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
Success in that it works and everyone on same chain

But some issues did arise that have been patched or are under investigation

the list (from my memory):
* teku made a bad block(s) -- issue self healed after 1 epoch and we know the problem. simple once found but tricky
* prysm launched without optimization flags and was seeing longer than expected times to produce block (think close to 1s instead of 300ms). optimizations are now deployed
* lighthouse was also seeing longer than expected block production times. not theory yet. australia went to sleep
* some very low sync committee blocks (e.g. 1% instead of 70%+)
* general lower than expected sync committee participation -- the missing bits are consistent block to block so seems like a systemic issue with a client or node rather than an issue with the algorithm. being investigated
